problems.reason: Sentence 1 claims adult Liliensternus could reach 7–9 m, while sentence 2 states it was only about 5.15 m long.
Sentences 7, 8 and 10 all repeat information about the discovery of the type specimens by Count Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern in the winter of 1932/1933.

Sentences 1, 2, and 3 give conflicting length estimates (7–9 m vs. ~5.15–5.20 m) and weight estimates (127 kg vs. 200 kg), while sentence 6 claims Liliensternus is one of the largest known theropods, which is inconsistent with the smaller size figures.
